reading.title: Movement Verbs 1: Adult Movement Class
reading.text: Nora likes to walk, jog or run in the park. An athlete may sprint; a marching group may march. Nora prefers to stroll. Outdoors she can hike, while a long difficult journey is a trek. Waiting, she may pace; long steps form a stride. At rehearsal she sees performers jump, hop, skip and leap. A ball can bounce.
reading.imageBrief: Adult observer beside a level park path or rehearsal floor with ordinary clear space. Narration supplies actions and speed; no specialist stunts, exercise prescriptions, cliff/water risks, arrows or readable text.

Which verb describes the short fast run?

Nora walks with long steps to stride. She does not jump into the air or hop on one foot.
Which verb describes walking with long steps?

At rehearsal Nora alternates a step and a hop to skip. A leap is a long or high jump; a ball may bounce after hitting the floor.
Which verb describes alternating a step and a hop?

What can bounce in the passage?
Say that you like to walk in the park.
exercises.answer: I like to walk in the park.
